title: Cloud attempts have no progress signal: the stall gap claims nothing without a local worktree
description:
The stall gap deliberately refuses to claim anything for an attempt whose worktree is not local, so a cloud-substrate attempt can stall for its whole wall clock with no early warning at all.

The measurement's honesty is the right default and should not be weakened: a local gap means a real observed gap. What is missing is a second, cloud-shaped progress fact that can stand in where the worktree cannot be read - the executor's own observation stream is the obvious candidate, with its last-observation timestamp as the idle signal.

Found by the 7zs worker while building the stall warning itself (run epic-9pd, tick 7zs, attempt 22).
acceptance_criteria: A cloud-substrate attempt that goes idle past the stall threshold raises the same stall_warned feed event a local one does, and a test proves it without a local worktree. The local gap measurement is unchanged for local attempts.
